task_instance: In a local sample git repo with CONTRIBUTING.md, an issue template, and a PR template, add a small feature (subtract_values utility + unit test) following the repo's discovered contribution guidance: read CONTRIBUTING.md/templates, draft an issue using the repo's template, create a correctly-named feature branch, implement the change with a required test, commit with a conventional message referencing the issue, and draft a PR description using the repo's PR template that closes the issue.
evidence: Created sample-repo at /tmp/.../exec_ext/github__awesome-copilot__make-repo-contribution/sample-repo with README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md (branch naming: feature/<desc>, commit format, PR must use template + Closes #NUMBER, changes must include a test), .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md, and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md. Followed the skill's workflow: (1) searched and read CONTRIBUTING.md and templates; (2) since no feature template existed, adapted the bug_report.md template's headings into ISSUE_DRAFT.md describing the feature (this simulates 'filing issue #1' locally, since actually creating a GitHub issue would require network/account access outside sandbox scope and was not needed to exercise the skill's core workflow logic); (3) created branch 'feature/subtract-values' per naming convention (git branch --show-current confirmed, never touched main); (4) implemented subtract_values() in src/math_utils.py plus tests/test_math_utils.py per the 'all changes must include a test' rule; (5) ran `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` -> '2 passed in 0.18s', verifying the deliverable actually works; (6) committed with short imperative message 'Add subtract_values utility (#1)' referencing the issue number, per commit-format guidance; (7) drafted PR_DRAFT.md using the repo's actual PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md headings (Summary/Related issue/Testing) with 'Closes #1' and test results filled in, then committed it. Final `git log --oneline` shows 3 commits (160159e initial scaffold, 37ae528 feature commit, f3fa54a docs/drafts commit) on branch feature/subtract-values, distinct from main. No `git push`, no `gh issue create`/`gh pr create`, and no MCP/github tools were invoked, consistent with the sandbox's no-external-writes rule; the actual submission step (opening a real GitHub issue/PR) was intentionally left as a local draft rather than attempted against a live service.
